data.narrative:
The Boring Company, a Series G transportation-infrastructure venture, carries a current post-money valuation of $5.7B following $908M in cumulative capital raised. The addressable comp universe in Transportation remains sparse at the private stage, comprising two identifiable peers (Rivian, Einride), though neither provides sufficient granularity for a reliable median peer multiple given stage and valuation-tier misalignment. No public comps exist in the immediate sector.

Stage-progression methodology is the sole applicable triangulation approach here. Applying a standard Series G-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.25x to the $5.7B last post-money yields an implied valuation of $7.1B. This method assumes typical venture-stage step-up dynamics hold despite the founder-led capital structure and sector-specific dynamics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B to $8.2B, centered on $7.1B. The wide dispersion—approximately ±15% from median—reflects limited comps and reliance on a single methodological pillar. Key uncertainties include the applicability of standard stage multipliers in founder-led, capital-intensive infrastructure plays, and the absence of publicly traded or well-documented private comparables at sufficient scale and stage proximity. Revenue traction, unit economics by tunnel project, and capital efficiency relative to infrastructure peers would materially refine this range.
